_comment: The eleven platform school subjects, in transcript order.
Canonical source of the KEYS and the display NAMES is
backend/utils/school_subjects.py (SCHOOL_SUBJECTS / SCHOOL_SUBJECT_DISPLAY_NAMES):
the keys are a database enum and the names are what a transcript line says.
The descriptions and accent colours are the clients' -- the backend has its
own SCHOOL_SUBJECT_DESCRIPTIONS written for quest creators, which is a
different audience and deliberately not this list.
Written 2026-09-07 (QF-01). Before it there were three hand-maintained
copies -- backend, frontend/src/constants/subjects.js, and
frontend-v2/src/components/class/SUBJECTS.ts -- and the web one carried a
comment asking whoever edited it to keep the other two in step, which is a
request that a person do a job a test should do. They had already drifted:
mobile described Language Arts as including world languages and the web did
not. Mobile's wording is used here, because it matches that file's own
documented naming rationale.
JSON rather than TypeScript for the same reason as pillars.json: a
CommonJS consumer cannot require a .ts module. shared/subjects.ts is the
typed front door for app code.
What is NOT here, because it belongs to one surface rather than to the
subject: mobile's Ionicons name, and the formal wording an official
transcript uses ('Mathematics', 'Physical Education', 'Career & Technical
Education'). A transcript says the long form on purpose; the pickers say the
short one. Both derive their KEY list from here, so a new subject cannot go
missing from either.

subjects.name: Language Arts
subjects.description: Reading, writing, storytelling, journalism, world languages

subjects.name: Science
subjects.description: Curiosity about how the world works

subjects.name: Electives
subjects.description: Anything else that sparks your interest
